title: Chronological queue slicers with fidelity erosion for tenant-aware load shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During regional load spikes and partial failures we need a tenant-aware load shedding mechanism that (1) preserves high-value/long-waiting requests, (2) degrades output fidelity in controlled steps, and (3) cooperates with multi-region failover and circuit breakers. Existing approaches are either coarse-grained (reject by tenant) or only model-quality based. Proposal: implement a two-stage runtime component: (A) chronological queue slicers — a slot-based admission allocator that slices queues by request arrival age and tenant priority, and (B) fidelity erosion profiles — configurable degradation ladders that progressively trim features (context length, sampling temperature, model variant, optional tool calls) with operator- and policy-driven thresholds. The combination aims to reduce p99 latency spikes and preserve SLOs for critical tenants while maximizing overall throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a slot allocator that enforces per-shard slot counts and slices queues by chronological bands (age windows) and tenant weight

Fidelity erosion profiles implemented with at least three steps: (1) context trim, (2) model fallback to smaller/quantized variant, (3) feature strip (disable tool calls/structured output) — adjustable per tenant and per region
Integrated with existing circuit-breaker signals: when upstream model errors > threshold or region latency spikes, admission moves to conservative slice and erosion step 2
Dashboard panels for slot utilization, age-band headroom, erosion-step fractions, and per-tenant SLO burn rate available in Console
Runbook automated actions: emergency rollback flag, per-tenant bypass list, and canary rollout via feature flag
No user-visible unseen regressions for top 20 customers in canary (regression tolerance: <1% increase in error budget burn)
E2E chaos test in staging simulates regional 40% capacity loss and proves 95% of priority requests succeed at erosion <= step 2
steps: Design: write a short design doc describing chronological bands, slot accounting, and sample erosion profiles (owner: Marco)
Prototype: implement in request router a slice calculator + slot token bucket (feature-flagged)
Integrate with admission control: wire slot allocation into the admission decision path and ensure KV cache lifetimes behave under trimmed context
Model-fallback wiring: ensure model catalog exposes shrink/quantized variants with compatibility checks
Observability: add metrics and Console graphs; hook SLO burn-rate alerts to erosion transitions
Testing: unit tests for allocator fairness, staging chaos test for multi-region failover, and load test comparing baseline vs slicer-enabled
Rollout: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with rollback on increased error-budget burn or p95 latency regressions
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting — aligned on chronology-first approach rather than strict priority-only queuing. Decided to keep tenant weights but prefer age protection to avoid starvation.
2026-02-26: Design doc v0 posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/chronological-queue-slicers — requested more detail on shard-local vs global slots (PM: Dana K).
2026-03-01: Engineering review — suggested simplification: use coarse age bands (0-200ms, 200-1s, 1s+) instead of dynamic percentile windows. Action: prototype with bands, measure distribution.
2026-03-04: UX/Console feedback from Evan R — need a single panel showing "erosion tax" by tenant and an operator toggle to move region into emergency-mode
2026-03-08: Prototype shows ~22% lower p99 under synthetic spike when protecting >500ms band and applying erosion step 1 for low-priority tenants. Iterating on thresholds.
2026-03-10: Security review not required for initial rollout; data handling unchanged. Preparing PR and staging runbook.
operator_runbook: Operator steps: (1) If Console shows erosion_step_fraction > 50% and SLO burn rising, toggle emergency-mode for affected region from the Console (operator toggle). (2) Use bypass list to temporarily exempt top customers and reroute traffic to Dedicated pools or alternate regions. (3) If circuit breaker trips in a region, set admission conservative mode which reduces per-tenant slots by 30% and advances erosion by +1 step. (4) Follow post-incident diagnostics: collect headroom histograms and per-tenant traces and open a postmortem if error budget exceeded by >2x.
notes_on_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: strict priority-only queues would protect high-paying tenants but starve others and increase overall SLO burn; chronological slicers reduce starvation for long-waiting requests but require accurate time skew handling and shard-local coordination. Fidelity erosion preserves request acceptance but may reduce perceived quality — we prioritize progressive degradation steps that are reversible and observable. We chose age bands for operational simplicity over continuous percentile windows to reduce flapping.
